newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Donors pledge $2.5 billion for Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Donors pledge $2.5 billion for Ethiopia.

text.p: Donor nations and institutions have pledged $2.5 billion towards Ethiopia's development strategy over the next three years, the World Bank's vice-president for Africa, Callisto Madavo, said on Thursday.

"The $2.5 billion which the donors pledge to provide Ethiopia during the 1996-99 period is in support of the ongoing development efforts with the ultimate aim of poverty reduction," Madavo told a news conference at the end of a three-day meeting of a consultative group of the donors in Addis Ababa.
The Ethiopian government had asked for $2 billion -- project financing of more than $1.3 billion and balance of payments support of not less than $600 million.
"The fact that donors pledged to give Ethiopia more than it asked for indicated the vote of confidence the donor community has in Ethiopia", Madavo said.

He said participants congratulated Ethiopia on its recent macroeconomic performance and said they hoped it would be sustained. But they also called on the government to accelerate public sector participation in its strategy, he added.

He said they noted the complexity of the decentralisation process in Ethiopia and urged the government "to move aggressively in implementing administrative and legal reforms to facilitate private-sector development".
Finance Minister Sufian Ahmed, who was also at the news conference, said Ethiopia was satisfied with the pledge. "It was more than we expected," he added.
He said the country's development strategy over the next three years would focus on the social sector -- improving primary education, primary health service and food security.
Neawye Gebreab, spcial adviser to the prime minister on economic affairs, said that with good rains and sound policies food production had increased over the last three years.

The Food and Agriculture Organisation estimates that cereal production in Ethiopia rose to 9.1 million tonnes in 1995/6, from seven million tonnes in 1994/95. Neawye said the estimate for the current 1996/97 period was that it would be 20 percent higher than in the previous year.
But he said that that despite the bumper harvest Ethiopia would need food aid for years to come.
Ethiopia received a pledge of $1.1 billion at a consultative group meeting in Paris in 1994.
